subject: PrivDeploy tenant admission & pre-warm retention policy review
messages:
From: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@embercloud.com
Date: 2026-10-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: PrivDeploy tenant admission & pre-warm retention policy review

Team,

Following up from the architecture sync — I sketched a proposal for how we should admit tenants into a private GPU pool and how long we keep pre-warmed allocations (retention) before reclaiming. Goal: balance predictable latency for priority customers with sensible utilization for multi-tenant private deployments. Please review and flag concerns/things to quantify.

High-level proposal (TL;DR):
- Priority tiers: P0 (SLA-critical), P1 (paid dedicated), P2 (best-effort/multi-tenant).
- Admission windows: P0 always admitted, P1 admitted if pool spare capacity >= 10% headroom after pre-warms, P2 admitted when spare >= 25%.
- Pre-warm retention: P0 persist pre-warm up to 14 days idle; P1 up to 48 hours; P2 2 hours.
- Grace eviction: scale-down only evicts P2 first, then P1 (with 1-hour eviction notice via webhook), never evict P0 unless manual override by operations.
- Throughput targets: target sustained throughput per GPU node = 750 tokens/sec for our quantized 70B profile; allow 15% burst headroom for scheduled jobs.
- Network/egress: cap tenant egress per vNIC to 300 Mbps to avoid cross-tenant noise; apply per-tenant burst bucket.

Metrics to validate in sim: 95/99/99.9 tail latency, prewarm hit-rate, eviction frequency per tier, average utilization, percent time we need to refuse admission.

Asks:
1) Priyom — run the admission sim (job + load synthesis) with 3 configurations: conservative (high retention), balanced (numbers above), aggressive (short retention) and report back with tail latencies.
2) Karthik — sanity-check the 750 tokens/sec baseline against your telemetry for the 70B quantized binary and the kernel choices.
3) Laura — any compliance/contractual constraints for P0 retention (esp. regulated customers)? Also want ops contact for manual-override etiquette.

I attached a short spreadsheet skeleton (admission-sim-outputs.csv) for sim outputs and a Drive link to the sim harness.

Thanks,
Mina

Subject: Re: PrivDeploy tenant admission & pre-warm retention policy review

Mina — thanks, this is a useful starting point. Quick notes after a quick pass and an initial sim run (attached baseline outputs in the CSV):

- I'll run the three configs you requested. First-pass results (balanced config) show average utilization ~72% and 99th pct latency at ~220ms for the 70B quantized profile at 750 tokens/sec baseline. 99.9th is at ~560ms during synthetic microbursts.
- Suggest instrumenting a "rejection backoff" test where we send admission requests that are requeued with exponential backoff so we can measure user-visible delay (not just immediate admission fail rate).
- We should add a canary flag that pins one node to P0-only pre-warms during canary windows to validate evictions under load without impacting all tenants.

Action: I'll land the sim configs into the Drive folder and push csv outputs by EOD tomorrow. Also pinging ops@embercloud.com for any known egress throttles on their side (cc'd).

- Priyom

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-30T09:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PrivDeploy tenant admission & pre-warm retention policy review

Thanks, Mina. Quick validation notes from kernel/profile side:

- 750 tokens/sec looks conservative for our quantized 70B with attention optimizations when sequence lengths are <= 512. With mixed sequence lengths (mean 700, heavy tails) we see effective throughput drop ~18-22%. For planning, use 620 tokens/sec as the working baseline for mixed workloads if we want to keep 99th < 300ms.
- Pre-warm retention recommendations: P0 10 days (not 14) — longer retention has high opportunity cost and little marginal latency improvement after day 7 in our sims. P1 36 hours instead of 48 (significant utilization gain). Keep P2 at 2 hours.
- Admission policy tweak: rather than absolute spare capacity thresholds, use a staged admission curve tied to current warm-hit rate: eg admit P1 when spare >= 8% AND warm-hit-rate > 70%. This reduces oscillation when prewarm churn is high.

I attached the sim outputs (admission-sim-outputs.csv) with the mixed-workload run and added a short summary in the Drive doc (link above). Also added a small section on network egress; the 300 Mbps cap is fine but we should consider per-tenant token-rate policing at the edge to avoid queue saturation during bursts.

Karthik

All — this is shaping up well. A couple of compliance/contract notes and next steps:

- P0 retention: for regulated customers we need to capture retention SLAs in the contract addendum (explicit max idle time and override window). I'll coordinate with legal and loop in the account team for EmberCloud if required.
- Ops manual override: we need a runbook. Ops should only perform a P0 eviction in emergency with an annotated ticket and auto-notification to customer reps.

Next steps / meetings:
1) Priyom to post full sim outputs and the rejection-backoff experiment by 2026-11-02.
2) Karthik to update the baseline throughput to 620 tokens/sec for mixed workloads and rerun the balanced config.
3) Mina to own the policy doc and PRIV-9142 ticket for rollout. I'll schedule a 45-minute review on 2026-11-03 10:00am PT — invite will go to this thread and EmberCloud ops (infra-procure cc'd for procurement constraints).

+1 on the canary node idea.

Thanks,
Laura
